title: Magic E
kidRule: A quiet E at the end of a word reaches back over one letter and makes the vowel say its own name. That is how the A in ESCAPE and the I in INVITE get to say their names! It works most of the time, but not in a few words like HAVE and GIVE.
hint: Listen to the vowel: it says its own name! What quiet helper at the very end of the word makes that happen?
reminder: The vowel says its own name, so a quiet E goes at the very end of the word.

check.question: Why does the A in ESCAPE say its own name?
check.correctAnswer: The quiet E at the end makes the vowel say its name!
distractors: Because A always says its name after the letter C
Because the letter P makes the vowel before it louder

words.def: To get away from a place where you were stuck or shut in.
words.sent: The hamster tried to escape from his cage.
words.story: An octopus has no bones, so it can escape through any hole that is bigger than its hard little beak!
words.card: The superhero's *cape* tried to *escape* from the washing machine!

words.def: To ask someone to come to a party or to do something with you.
words.sent: I will invite my whole class to the picnic.
words.story: The letters RSVP on a party invitation stand for French words that mean 'please reply'!
words.card: I will *invite* a penguin to sleep *in* our freezer!

words.def: Something you did wrong without meaning to.
words.sent: I made a mistake and put salt in my cocoa.
words.story: The ice pop was invented by mistake! In 1905 an eleven-year-old boy named Frank left his fruity drink outside on a cold night with the stirring stick still in it.
words.card: Oops! It was a *mistake* to *take* a cactus to the balloon party!

words.def: Special clothes you wear to look like someone or something else.
words.sent: My costume for the play is a fuzzy bee suit.
words.story: Actors in a big musical sometimes have to change costume in less than a minute, with helpers waiting just offstage!
words.card: My pickle *costume* *cost* three cookies and a high five!

words.def: Having all its parts, with nothing missing.
words.sent: My sticker book is finally complete.
words.story: It takes Earth about 365 days to complete one trip around the Sun. That is what we call a year!
words.card: My tower of one hundred pancakes is *complete*, so *let* us eat!

words.def: A long brass horn you play by sliding a tube in and out.
words.sent: My sister plays the trombone in the school band.
words.story: The name of this horn comes from Italian and means 'big trumpet'!
words.card: The dog buried a *bone* inside the *trombone*, and now it only plays woofs!

words.def: To tell what someone or something is like, using words.
words.sent: Can you describe the puppy you saw?
words.story: Scientists describe thousands of newly discovered kinds of animals every year, and most of them are insects!
words.card: The baby tried to *describe* the monster under her *crib*: fuzzy, purple and very polite!

words.def: To make something look prettier by adding things to it.
words.sent: We decorate the classroom with paper stars.
words.story: A male bowerbird likes to decorate the ground around his nest with blue things he collects, such as berries, flowers and bottle caps!
words.card: A *rat* helped me *decorate* the cake with tiny cheese stars!

words.def: A tube with special glass that makes faraway things, like stars, look bigger and closer.
words.sent: Through the telescope I could see the rings of Saturn.
words.story: About 400 years ago, Galileo pointed a telescope at Jupiter and discovered four of its moons!
words.card: The pirate's *telescope* could not *cope* with a seagull sitting on the end!

words.def: An animal covered in long, sharp spikes called quills.
words.sent: The porcupine raised its quills when the dog came near.
words.story: A porcupine has about 30,000 quills, and its name comes from old words meaning 'spiny pig'!
words.card: The *porcupine* hugged a *pine* tree because nobody else was brave enough!
